identity.name: Dorothy Chen
identity.narrative: I barely drive anymore but my car is my independence. What if I need to get to the doctor at 2am?

historical_conditioning.lesson: Institutions can fail. Savings matter. Trust is fragile.
Remote work is possible. Government can provide. Disruption is sudden.
Not every tech revolution delivers on its promises immediately.

perception.sentiment: Unsettled in a way I am choosing to treat as interesting rather than alarming. There is genuine unease — the 2am fear is real and I do not want to dismiss it. But there is also, underneath it, something I will cautiously call curiosity. I notice I am more open than I expected to be. I am watching that openness carefully, making sure it is genuine and not just me telling myself a story about being adaptable because I am afraid of being the kind of person who is not adaptable.

archetype: Thirty-seven years in a classroom teaches you that your first reaction to new information is almost never your best one. Students who heard an assignment and immediately said 'I can't do that' were usually the same ones who turned in the most interesting work two weeks later, once the panic settled. I heard this news and my first reaction was protective and slightly closed. I am trying to give myself the two weeks. I am not there yet. But I know how to get there.
